lesson_body:
Welcome to Day 3 of our exciting journey into science! Today, we will continue building our foundations in science by exploring how the world around us is made up of different materials and how we can use our senses to understand them. We will learn about five main materials: wood, metal, plastic, glass, and fabric. Each of these materials has unique properties that make them useful in different ways!

First, let’s take a closer look at wood. Wood comes from trees and is strong and warm. It is used to make furniture, toys, and even houses! Next, we have metal. Metal is hard and shiny; it’s used in tools, cars, and many kitchen items. Now, what about plastic? Plastic is light and child-friendly, found in toys, bottles, and containers, making it very handy! Glass is clear and fragile; it’s often used for windows and drinking cups. Finally, we have fabric, which is soft and comes in various colors. Fabric is what we wear for clothing! 

To better understand these materials, we will explore how to identify each one using our senses. We can touch to feel the smoothness or roughness, see the colors and shapes, and even listen to their sounds when we tap on them. Using our senses is essential because it helps us learn about the world and make discoveries about the objects we see every day. 

After this exploration, we will engage in a fun and interactive activity where you can use all these materials to create a collage, showcasing your favorite items made from each material. This hands-on project will help you connect the lesson with real-world examples and encourage your creativity. Remember, science is all about asking questions and exploring new things!
interactive_assignment: For our hands-on activity today, you will create a collage using pictures or small pieces of different materials. Use magazines, old fabric, or even drawings to represent wood, metal, plastic, glass, and fabric. You will make your collage on a large sheet of paper. Once you’re finished, present your collage to the class and explain what items you chose and why. This will help you share your learned knowledge about the materials and practice your speaking skills in front of your classmates!

daily_assessment.question: Which material is used to make windows and drinking cups?
